clue.text: Secure harbour that's a demilitarised area

parts.note: secure means safe, free from danger
a haven is a harbour or port

explanation.surface: A protected port turns out to be a zone where no troops are stationed.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge zone declared off-limits to fighting is the political sense of the phrase, a protected area without armed forces.

clue.text: Crab's dodgy movement?

parts.note: crabs scuttle sideways, and a dodging step to one side is what a boxer or footballer makes to avoid a challenge

explanation.definitionFit: A dodge to the side, the evasive step that matches the way a crab walks.

clue.text: Get off successfully with good wishes at parting

definitions.meaning: to get on or get off well is to do well, as in a phrase for doing well on a journey
the words said when someone leaves, a goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone escapes with luck and receives a fond send-off.
explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means to get on well or prosper; as one it is a goodbye, the wishes said on leaving.

clue.text: Henry VIII's stature?

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
VIII is the Roman numeral for eight

explanation.surface: A question about how tall the Tudor king Henry VIII was.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one king's name; split it into Henry, giving H, and the numeral VIII, giving EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is how tall a person stands, their vertical measurement.

clue.text: Thoroughly acquainted poetically?

definitions.meaning: to be well up in a subject, skilled and knowledgeable in it
put into lines of poetry, written in metre

explanation.surface: Someone knows a subject thoroughly, in a poetic way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well up in a subject is one sense; the other is set in metre, written as poetry.

clue.text: No lacework everyone finished? Never

parts.note: to tat is to make lace by hand, and tatting is that lacework
all means everyone, and also finished, as in 'the milk is all gone'

explanation.surface: Nobody has finished any lace yet, and the answer to whether they ever will is no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyone finished' both point to ALL: everyone is all, and finished is all as in 'it's all over'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal, meaning in no way whatsoever, the same force as a flat 'never'.

clue.text: Was upsetting jolly throng

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over and disordering, so the letters of Was are jumbled

parts.note: a jolly is crossword slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: An upsetting event seemed to delight a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' rearranges WAS into SWA; a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a dense crowd, and a swarm is a large moving mass of people or insects.

clue.text: Fish that have been packed?

parts.note: small oily fish famously packed tightly in tins, and also the party game where players squeeze together into one hiding place

explanation.definitionFit: Small fish sold tightly packed in a tin, the image behind the phrase 'packed like' them.

clue.text: One vote on the other side

parts.note: one is the article a
a voter marks the ballot with a cross

explanation.surface: A single ballot is cast for the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the way, to or on the far side of something, as a street.

clue.text: One found during Monday, say, or a Thursday

indicators.note: found during means placed inside, so the letter is set within the other piece
say signals the word is to be heard, giving a spelling that matches how it is spoken

parts.note: Monday is commonly pronounced 'Mundy'
one is the article a

explanation.surface: Someone discovered on a Monday, or possibly on a Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' gives the spoken form of Monday, MUNDY, and 'found during' puts A inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thursday before Easter is named for it, when the British monarch gives out special coins to pensioners.

clue.text: Director going along the row that is less clear

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: A film director walks along a row of seats that is less clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Murkier, more muddied and so harder to see through, the comparative of grubby.

clue.text: Withdraw from competition viewing area collapsed

parts.note: a stand is the grandstand where spectators watch a match
something collapsed has fallen down

explanation.surface: A grandstand fell down, so the event was abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out of a contest or step aside from a position, an idiom for resigning.

clue.text: Entertained as one was in hospital perhaps

definitions.meaning: entertained means paid for someone's meal or drink, stood them a round

definitions.text: as one was in hospital perhaps
definitions.meaning: describing a patient given medical care by doctors

explanation.surface: Someone was well looked after in hospital, entertained even.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to stand someone a drink or meal; the other is to have received medical care.

clue.text: Pardon lady going round home

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: Amy is a woman's name
a nest is a home, as for birds

explanation.surface: A woman asks forgiveness as she walks round her house.
explanation.definitionFit: A general pardon granted by a government, letting offenders off punishment.

clue.text: Protection in another country from capitalism you'll arrange

indicators.note: arrange tells the solver to put these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A dissident fleeing communism seeks shelter abroad, from capitalism's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' shuffles the letters of CAPITALISM YOU'LL, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuge granted by a foreign state to someone fleeing persecution in their homeland.

clue.text: Imposing governments get revenue from it

definitions.text: Imposing governments get revenue from it

parts.words: Imposing governments get revenue from it
parts.note: read 'imposing' as the verb: by levying it, states raise money, rather than as an adjective for grand governments

explanation.definitionFit: Levying duties and charges on citizens is how a state raises income.

clue.text: Rhythmical edition rotter enclosed first

indicators.note: first says the rotter and enclosed pieces come before the edition

parts.note: a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man
ENC is the abbreviation for enclosed or enclosure, as at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A rhythmic edition of a book has a scoundrel's note enclosed at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' moves the rotter and enclosed pieces before ED, though the clue names edition first.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a regular beat or measured fall in sound, as of verse or speech.

clue.text: No fellow at loggerheads with one who prefers his own company

definitions.text: one who prefers his own company

indicators.note: at loggerheads means in conflict and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Nobody quarrels with a man who prefers to be alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a person who keeps apart from others and likes solitude.

clue.text: Methods tally oddly in an unpretentious way

parts.note: modes are methods or ways of doing something

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word tally

explanation.surface: Methods that add up strangely are presented without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes letters one, three and five of TALLY, giving TLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbly, without showing off or making a fuss about oneself.

clue.text: About fifty, having had cut, took it easy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
axed means cut, as a job or budget

explanation.surface: A man of about fifty who has lost his job finally takes it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest and unwind, letting the tension go; the past tense matches 'took'.

clue.text: Go up astronomically?

parts.note: prices that soar are said to shoot up; read literally, it is a missile launched into space

explanation.definitionFit: To soar dramatically, as prices do, like a craft blasting off into space.

clue.text: Many to draw lady, shortly

parts.note: a lot means many
a tie is a draw, a match with no winner

explanation.surface: Many people come to sketch a woman, briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet form of the girl's name Charlotte, so a lady's name in short form.

clue.text: Gathered a legend needs translating

indicators.note: translating means rendering in other form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone collected an old myth that must be put into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect bit by bit, as stray grain after the harvest or scraps of information.

clue.text: Chap from Armagh

indicators.note: from suggests a name made out of the letters of the place, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A man who comes from the Northern Irish town of Armagh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' signals the shuffle: the man is made out of the letters of ARMAGH, a town in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A common first name for a man, so a chap's name.

clue.text: Reveal that Kevin certainly is content

indicators.note: content means the inside of something, so the answer is the letters held within these words

explanation.surface: Kevin certainly is happy, and wants to show it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like Kevin's mood; it means contents, the letters inside 'Kevin certainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To show plainly, make evident a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Jazz fan carries a weight, one with a type of schizophrenia

indicators.note: carries means is followed by the next pieces, the fan bearing them along

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a ton is a unit of weight
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A jazz lover struggling with a heavy load turns out to have a mental illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carries' joins the jazz fan to A TON; 'one with a' gives I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of stupor and rigidity, once classed as a subtype of the mental illness.

clue.text: Spend one's time in suspense?

definitions.meaning: to frequent a place, pass time there, an informal phrasal verb
read literally, to be suspended outside, as washing on a line

explanation.surface: Someone passes their time waiting anxiously for news.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to idle somewhere habitually; literally, to be suspended outdoors like washing.

clue.text: Little in outskirts of town in intermediate place

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of town

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small village lies on the edge of a town, between places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outskirts of' takes the first and last letters of TOWN, giving TN, and 'in' puts WEE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened form of between, meaning in the middle position.

clue.text: Maiden with knowing little creature

parts.note: a damsel is a maiden, a young woman
fly is British slang for knowing, sharp or streetwise

explanation.surface: A young woman with a knowing look beside a small animal.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY is British slang for shrewd and hard to fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender insect related to the dragonfly, a small winged creature.
